newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF in Ukraine to discuss new $2.5-$3 billion EFF.
newsitem.headline: IMF in Ukraine to discuss new $2.5-$3 billion EFF.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund mission has arrived in Ukraine for talks on a new, $2.5-3.0 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF), an IMF official said on Monday.

"They are in the process of working on the EFF deal and they are concentrating on the budget. The talks are dedicated to 'Article Four' consultations," the official said, referring to talks the Fund holds every year with credit recipients.
Ukraine's parliament is due to hold its first full session of 1997 on Tuesday and speaker Olexander Moroz said last week the draft budget could be passed in March.

Tamara Kutsai, spokeswoman for Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Pynzenyk who is in charge of economic reform, said the new credit could be agreed and the first money paid out a month after the budget was passed.

The mission, which arrived on January 29 and is due to leave on February 7, is meeting officials from the central bank and the ministries of economy, finance, foreign trade and foreign affairs, an official close to the talks said.

Ukraine has already received most of a $860 million stand-by loan which is due to expire this month and should soon get the ninth and final tranche, worth about $100 million, another official close to the talks said.
The IMF talks are also expected to concentrate on much-needed tax reforms which Kuchma has asked parliament to pass quickly to increase budget revenues.
